Two things to pin.

1. `wrapGraceOpen(collab, now, graceMs)`. Model it on the `claimLapsed` and `claimRecording` tests that already sit around line 172-197 — same shape, same commenting voice, same use of the `NOW` constant the file already defines. Cover, at minimum: a wrapped room inside the grace admits; exactly on the boundary admits (the predicate is `<=`, deliberately inclusive — say so, and pin it, the way the sibling test pins `claimRecording`'s inclusive `>=`); one millisecond past refuses; a non-`wrapped` status refuses whatever the clock says (walk the other four — open, live, wrapping, closed — so the predicate cannot quietly widen into a phase test); a wrapped row whose `wrapped_at` is absent, null or unparseable REFUSES. 2. The clock ordering. The file already has a test named 'the three session clocks keep their ordering'. Add the wrap-window ordering: `WRAP_GRACE_MS + UPLOAD_URL_TTL_MS < WRAPPED_TTL_MS` strictly, so a take admitted at the very last moment of the commit window can never outlive the retention that is supposed to hold it — the grace must fit inside the promise, never extend it. Your call whether that goes in the existing test (rename its title if you widen it — 'the three session clocks' would then be wrong) or a new one beside it; either is fine, say which you chose and why. Every assertion carries its actual values in the message, as the existing ordering assertions do.

Both constants and the predicate need adding to the import list at the top of the file.
